title: Ride vs Pin vs Submission
shortDefinition: Three different phases: ride to expose the back, pin to stabilize the position, submission to finish.
whyItMatters: Confusing ride with pin makes you lose the back or submission when you have good control.
deepExplanation: Ride is moving with reactions to find the back (turtle, crab, wrist ride). Pin is stabilizing hip and shoulder lines (side, mount). Submission is isolating a specific line. Wrong phase breaks the system.
advancedView: Transition phases smoothly: ride → back exposure → pin → submission. Do not skip phases.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Ride vs Pin vs Submission during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Ride vs Pin vs Submission to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Ride vs Pin vs Submission is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Ride vs Pin vs Submission before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
